course.description: Build a reusable Cowork task that cross-references a client folder against your required documents checklist and drafts a polished follow-up email for anything outstanding — so nothing gets missed at deadline time.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Set Up the Missing Docs Tracker Skill in Claude Cowork.

lessons.content:
The **Missing Docs Tracker** skill is a saved Cowork task that checks a client folder against your required documents list and drafts a professional follow-up email for anything that's missing — so you never chase documents manually.

**What it handles:**
- Cross-references the contents of a client folder against your standard required documents checklist
- Identifies missing, incomplete, or expired documents
- Prioritises the gaps (critical vs. nice-to-have)
- Drafts a polished, professional follow-up email addressed to the client requesting the outstanding items

**Why build it as a skill:** Every client engagement has the same document requirements — save the checklist once and run it at intake or deadline time.
lessons.title: What this skill does

lessons.content:
1. Open **Claude Cowork** on your desktop
2. Click **New Task**
3. Name it: **Missing Docs Tracker**
4. Leave the task open — the next step is where you write the instructions that make this a real skill

> **Note:** In Cowork, a "skill" is simply a task with good instructions. The name you give it is what you'll see every time you open it. Keep it short and descriptive — "Missing Docs Tracker" is perfect.
lessons.title: Create the task in Cowork

activities.title: Write the skill instructions (this is the skill)

lessons.content:
In the task instructions field, paste the prompt below. **Replace the required documents list with your firm's actual checklist — this is the core of the skill.**

---

*"You are my Missing Docs Tracker. Each time I run this task, I will either upload a list of documents in a client folder, or describe what I have received so far.*

*Cross-reference what I provide against this required documents checklist — replace with your actual list:*

*Required documents:*
- *Signed engagement letter → Replace with your firm's standard*
- *Previous year tax return*
- *All bank statements for the period*
- *Payslips or income summary (all employers)*
- *Group certificate / payment summary*
- *Dividend statements*
- *Rental income and expense records (if applicable)*
- *Loan statements*
- *Receipts for work-related deductions*
- *Private health insurance statement*
- *Superannuation statements*
- *Any notices of assessment from prior year*

*For each missing or incomplete item:*
- *Mark it as CRITICAL (lodgement cannot proceed without it) or HELPFUL (can proceed but may affect outcome) → Adjust these categories to match your firm's triage approach*

*Then draft a professional follow-up email to the client:*
- *Tone: polite, clear, not rushed*
- *List only CRITICAL items in the subject line*
- *List all missing items in the body with a brief explanation of why each is needed*
- *Include a deadline — I will tell you the date, or use [DATE] as a placeholder*
- *Sign off as: [Your name] — replace with your name or firm name"*

---

> **Make it yours:** Add engagement-type variations (e.g. business clients vs. individuals), adjust the tone to match your firm's communication style, and include your firm's contact details in the sign-off.
lessons.title: Write the skill instructions (this is the skill)

activities.title: Run it and save your skill

lessons.content:
# Run it and save your skill

You've built the task — now run it and lock it in.

## Run your first missing docs check

1. Open Cowork and navigate to your **Missing Docs Tracker** task
2. Provide a sample client folder listing and your required documents checklist
3. Hit **Run** and review the output:
   - Does it correctly identify what's missing vs. what's present?
   - Is the follow-up email draft professional and specific to the gaps found?
   - Would you be comfortable sending that email to a client as-is?

## If something's off

Edit the task instructions — be more specific about:
- Exactly how your client folders are named or structured
- The tone of your follow-up emails (formal, friendly, urgent)
- Whether you want one email per client or a summary list

Re-run until the output matches your standard.

## Save it as a reusable skill

Once you're happy with the output:
- **Rename the task** to something clear: e.g. `Missing Docs Tracker — Tax Season`
- Pin it or star it so it's quick to access when onboarding a new client file
- If you have different document lists for different client types, clone the task and adjust per client category

## You now have a repeatable process

Every client file: open the task, paste the folder contents, get the gap report and a ready-to-send email. No manual cross-referencing. No chasing docs you already have.
